_read_me: Copy this file to content/posting/config.json in your project and change it there. Keys starting with _ are notes and are ignored.
_slots: One entry per kind of post. days: which weekdays get a slot. time: local time. max_per_day: how many of this kind one day may carry. second_offset_h: when a missed leg moves onto a day that already has one, how many hours after the first it goes. The starting times below are a stagger to try (the long-form-friendly platform first, the others a few hours later), not a measured best time for your audience.
_hand_platforms: Platforms the machine never posts to. They get a hand card and a reminder instead. TikTok and Substack are here by default: neither offers a posting API a tool like this may use for your own account.
_adapters: route: composio (the easy option: Composio's CLI with your connected accounts), direct (stubs, untested), or fake (a pretend platform for a first practice week). composio_account: the id of the one connected account to use, so a second account can never be picked by mistake. expected_account_id: YOUR OWN channel, member or user id, read with `runner.py whoami <platform>`; the runner reads the connected account before every upload and refuses unless it matches. When you switch a platform off fake, replace fake-creator with your real id and delete account_id.
_hosting: Instagram fetches your video from a public https URL. Either put file_url (and thumb_url) on the leg yourself, or name a command that uploads a file, and the public address it lands at. {file} is the full path, {key} is <date>/<file name>.
_reminder: Optional. A command the watcher runs to remind you of a hand post. {text} is replaced by the reminder. The example shows a desktop notification on a Mac.
_reminder_example_mac: display notification "{text}" with title "Time to post"
